words.gram: masculine accusative singular inanimate demonstrative pronoun

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'I', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: С возвращением тебя к нам, Витя!
examples.trans: Welcome back to us, Vitya!
But a special thank you to my son-in-law.

examples.text: Папа, он пока ещё не зять.
examples.trans: Dad, he is not your son-in-law yet.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'not', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Папа, он пока ещё не зять.
examples.trans: Dad, he is not your son-in-law yet.
Vitya, you must not get nervous at all.
I actually like this idea.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'can, am able to', paired with 'смочь'.

examples.trans: I can't today.
That can't be.

examples.text: Этого не может быть. Это наша история.
examples.trans: That can't be. It's our history.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to speak', paired with 'сказать'.

examples.trans: I wanted to talk with you.
Gulya, I cannot talk right now.
And you and I will have a talk.

meanings.note: Prefix 'под-' ('under, up to') indicates approaching or supporting from below (stem 'ождать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'wait', paired with 'ждать'.

examples.trans: Wait, I'll be right there.
Wait a minute.

examples.text: Подожди, Нин, ты не поняла. Это же стыдно!
examples.trans: Wait, Nina, you don't get it. It's shameful!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'this, it (is)', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: That title will be his in twenty-four hours.
This is our new head chef.
Really, and who is this man?

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'ейчас').

examples.trans: Heavy work is forbidden for you right now.
Believe me, right now it is not too late.

examples.text: Парни, сейчас всё в ваших руках.
examples.trans: Guys, everything is in your hands right now.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'very', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: And he is a very interesting man.
Alright, Mom, I am very glad.
Wait, this is very important right now.

meanings.note: Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('important, mattering').

examples.trans: Wait, this is very important right now.
I must make an important announcement.
It's an important question.

meanings.en: to try, to attempt, to make an effort
meanings.note: Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'tried', paired with 'попытаться'.

examples.trans: I tried!
He tried to explain the situation.

examples.text: Пыталась? С бутылкой вина в руке?
examples.trans: You tried? With a bottle of wine in your hand?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'to you', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: You will handle general supervision.
You look simply like a princess.
Just do not scare me.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'егодня').

examples.trans: Let us hold a fair duel today.
Let us leave here together today.
Chef, we will tear them apart today!

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'казать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to say', paired with 'говорить'.

examples.trans: I tried to tell you today.
I already told Katya about you.
What did you say?

meanings.en: to leave, go away, depart (by transport)
meanings.note: Prefix 'у-' marks departure, removal, or successful completion (stem 'езжать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'am leaving', paired with 'уехать'.

examples.trans: I am leaving for Bishkek forever.
Wait, what do you mean you are leaving?

examples.text: Уезжай с Алёшей на шесть месяцев.
examples.trans: Go away with Alyosha for six months.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'in, into', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: С возвращением тебя к нам, Витя!
examples.trans: Welcome back to us, Vitya!
Misha, thank you for everything.
And thank you all very much.

meanings.note: Prefix 'на-' marks surface contact, accumulation, or completing a quantity (stem 'всегда').

examples.trans: I am leaving for Bishkek forever.
Leave this place forever!
They parted forever.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian expressive spoken interjection meaning 'farewell', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Я пришёл попросить у тебя прощения.
examples.trans: I came to ask your forgiveness.
Farewell, Lyova, do not look for me.
Farewell, Denis, and be happy.

meanings.note: Prefix 'ис-' ('out from within') marks extraction or exhaustion (stem 'кать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'look for'.

examples.trans: I'm looking for a job.
What are you looking for?

examples.text: Ну что, довольна? Теперь новую работу искать.
examples.trans: Well, happy now? Now I have to look for a new job.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'how', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: You look simply like a princess.
Denis, how did you get in here?
Let us do it like in the old days!

meanings.note: Prefix 'про-' indicates movement through, completion, or missing the mark (stem 'стить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'forgive', paired with 'прощать'.

examples.trans: Chef, forgive me for the dish.
Forgive me, please, for everything.
Forgive me, our wedding is called off today.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'for', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Misha, thank you for everything.
Heavy work is forbidden for you right now.

examples.text: Всю жизнь я за тебя боялась.
examples.trans: All my life I was afraid for you.

meanings.note: Common neuter noun meaning 'dish' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Each pair will prepare one dish.
Chef, forgive me for the dish.
I do, and what does that mean?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'where to', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: And where will we go?
Anywhere at all, choose for yourself.
Lyova, where are you running off to now?

meanings.en: to break into a run, to run off
meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'бежать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'ran', paired with 'бежать'.

examples.trans: Lyova, where are you running off to now?
That is it, I am running off to the bachelorette party.

examples.text: Схватил собачку в парке и побежал.
examples.trans: Grab the little dog in the park and run.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'мотреть'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'watch', paired with 'посмотреть'.

examples.trans: I want to look at my cooks.
Look what I've got.
I'm watching TV.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'forward', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Look ahead, open your eyes wide!
Go ahead.

examples.text: Вы взяточник! Вы лезете вперёд больного ребёнка.
examples.trans: You're a bribe-taker! You're pushing in ahead of a sick child.

meanings.note: Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'open wide'.

examples.trans: Look ahead, open your eyes wide!

examples.text: Надо всё сделать и разуть вовремя.
examples.trans: We need to do everything and open wide on time.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronominal determiner meaning 'one's own (my, your, his...)', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: I want to look at my cooks.
He brought his own team here.
Go and win back your jobs.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'eyes' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: This is our new head chef.
Look ahead, open your eyes wide!
I agree, but how?

meanings.note: Prefix 'про-' indicates movement through, completion, or missing the mark (stem 'должать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to continue', paired with 'продолжить'.

examples.trans: There is no point in continuing the duel now.
We're continuing the operation.
Go on, I'm listening.

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'единок'). Formed with a diminutive/expressive Slavic suffix adding warmth or small scale. Common masculine noun meaning 'duel / match' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Let us hold a fair duel today.
There is no point in continuing the duel now.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'already', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: All of that is already in the past.
There is no point in continuing the duel now.
Wait, have we arrived already?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'no', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: No, I am speaking seriously.
Whoever cooks better will stay.
There is no point in continuing the duel now.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'мысл'). Common masculine noun meaning 'sense, meaning' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: There is no point in continuing the duel now.
What do you mean?
There's no sense in it.

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'шутить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'was joking, joked', paired with 'шутить'.

examples.trans: Gulya, tell me, were you joking just now?
If you were joking, it is not funny.

examples.text: Я смотрю, вы легковерный! Я же пошутила!
examples.trans: I see you're gullible! I was only joking!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian clause-linking conjunction meaning 'if', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: If you were joking, it is not funny.
Come if you want.
And if not?

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'мешно'). Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: If you were joking, it is not funny.
Do you find it funny?
That's very funny.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'they', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: They cook much better than you.
They lost this battle.
They stole my wedding dress!

meanings.note: Prefix 'про-' indicates movement through, completion, or missing the mark (stem 'играть'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'lost', paired with 'проигрывать'.

examples.trans: They lost this battle.
I lost it on the stock exchange.
Our team lost.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronominal determiner meaning 'this', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: That title will be his in twenty-four hours.
This is our new head chef.
Really, and who is this man?

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'fight, combat, battle' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: I wanted to talk with you.
They lost this battle.
And you and I will have a talk.
